home.lead: We are all brothers and sisters, from New York to Kyiv, from Moscow to Tokyo, from Rome to Sydney.
home.sub: A simple, nonviolent and nonpartisan place that gives voice to the people: people from every country can make themselves heard, with verifiable facts and mutual respect.

manifesto.title: The manifesto
manifesto.intro: We have different names, families, jobs, fears and hopes. We all want the same thing: to live with dignity, in peace, and to leave our children a better world than the one we found.

principles.title: Against violence
principles.text: No unjustified violence is acceptable, whichever side it comes from and whoever it is aimed at: protesters, police, institutions or individuals. We condemn violence, never a people or a nationality.

principles.title: The voice of the people
principles.text: Power belongs to the people and is exercised through speech, the vote, work and solidarity, never through fear. Everyone has the right to be heard and to dissent peacefully.

principles.title: Dignity is not for sale
principles.text: A person's dignity cannot be bought or bargained away. It is true for someone in New York as in Kyiv, in Moscow as in Tokyo, in Rome as in Sydney.

principles.title: Facts first
principles.text: Every figure we publish has a source, a date and a link. We separate what is verified from opinion and testimony, and we attribute partisan figures to whoever gives them.

principles.title: We are not a party
principles.text: We serve no political party and use no party symbols. We do not attack people: we discuss problems.

principles.title: Growing together
principles.text: We want a world of shared growth, not division. The wellbeing of a few is not enough: we work so that life gets better for everyone.

manifesto.note: The manifesto is declaratory: it is not a legal act and gives no legal protection to those who sign up to it.

places.title: Where we are
places.intro: The site has two levels: a global voice and a section for each country or cause.

itsud.title: Southern Italy
itsud.text: The first section: young people, farmers and citizens of Southern Italy. News, data and voices, always with sources.

francia.title: France
francia.text: A movement that began in high schools has widened to the cost of living. Timeline, government and organisers' figures, and the positions of each side, with sources.

next.title: Your country
next.text: Would you like a section for your country or your cause? Propose it with a simple form: we need the country, the situation in a few lines and a few public sources.

itsud.slogan: ITALIA, RICORDA CHI È IL TUO PADRONE: IL POPOLO!
itsud.intro: Facts, data and voices about the situation of young people, farmers and citizens in Southern Italy. Every entry has a date, a source and a link. We separate facts from opinions and attribute partisan figures to whoever supplies them.
itsud.nonviolence: This site gives voice to the people, supports peaceful forms of protest and condemns all violence, whichever side it comes from.

requests.title: The demands and the state of the responses
requests.intro: What farmers are asking for and what has been done so far. For legislation, the texts published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale are authoritative.

stats.title: The data
stats.intro: Each figure shows its period, the body that produced it and its source. Monthly figures are volatile: always check the date.

howToRead.title: How to read this page
items: Fact: an event or a figure with a verifiable source.
Partisan figure: a number given by an organisation (for example "according to Coldiretti"), not independently confirmed.
Source to be rechecked: we have not yet compared this entry with the original document.

contribute.title: Do you have news, a figure or an error to report?
contribute.text: Propose an entry with a source that can be checked, or report an error: the forms guide you and no personal data is needed.

francia.intro: Since late September 2026, protests that began in high schools over school conditions have widened to students, unions and the Gilets jaunes against the cost of living. The 17 October mobilisation was the largest so far, with clashes, fires and many arrests. Here you will find facts, figures and the positions of each side, each with its source: where numbers differ we report them all, attributed.
francia.nonviolence: This site gives voice to the people, supports peaceful forms of protest and condemns all violence, whichever side it comes from: protesters, police, institutions or anyone else; against people, schools and public buildings, and against those who demonstrate. We also report the criticism of the use of force against minors, and the government's positions.
francia.sourcesNote: Sources are in French and English; the summaries are our own.

requests.title: The demands and the responses
requests.intro: What high-school and university students are asking for and what the government has answered, according to the sources. The two sides do not always agree on what has been done.

stats.title: The numbers
stats.intro: Where figures differ you will find the government's and the organisers', each attributed: they are partisan counts, not independently verified.
